summary: Tested new Curriculum Gradebook Grid (GET /api/reports/gradebook) + frontend grid in /teacher-reports. Backend: 12/12 pytest tests pass (happy path shape, column ordering rules, per-column cell completeness, empty classroom rows=[], 404 unknown classroom, 404 for classroom owned by another teacher, 401/403 unauthenticated, 422 missing param, no _id leak, manual lesson-avg math verification against MongoDB, regression of legacy POST /reports/gradebook and POST /reports/missing). Frontend: logged in as admin teacher, default report type is 'Curriculum Gradebook (grid view)', classroom select + Load Gradebook render a 92-column x 2/5-row grid; sticky first column verified (x unchanged after scrollLeft=18022) and sticky header row verified (y unchanged with forced vertical overflow); all data-testids present; Excel download works (Gradebook_Test Classroom_2026-08-28.xlsx); switching to Grade Report mode cleanly hides the grid (no regression). One real visual defect found: the sticky student-name column has a semi-transparent background so scrolled score cells bleed through behind student names.

minor.issue: Columns are derived from EVERY document in db.problems globally (no teacher/curriculum-ownership filter), producing 92 columns including near-duplicate chapter names ('Chapter 1: Block Basics' vs 'Chapter 1: First Steps') and lesson-like entries such as 'Basics Quiz'. Consider scoping problems to the curriculum/chapters actually assigned to the classroom or owned by the teacher.

lesson_avg treats every problem with no submission as 0, so a student who never opened a lesson shows a red '0' instead of blank/not-attempted (whole grid was 0 for the test classes). Only lesson quiz / chapter test cells use null. Confirm this is the intended semantic; if not, return null when the student has zero submissions in the lesson.
Role-403 branch (student token) was NOT exercised — no student credentials available in /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Code path exists (user['role'] != 'teacher' -> 403) but is untested.

ui_bugs.component: TeacherReports curriculum grid — sticky student column
ui_bugs.issue: Sticky <td> uses `bg-inherit` which resolves to the row's semi-transparent bg (computed rgba(15,23,42,0.4)). Scrolled score cells show through the frozen column, rendering e.g. 'Amy Stapp0' / stray '0' glyphs inside the student-name column while scrolling horizontally. Fix: give the sticky cell an opaque background (e.g. bg-[#0f172a] / bg-cyber-navy, alternating opaque shades) instead of bg-inherit.

issues: 'Curriculum Gradebook will show:' heading and its bullet list render in a dim blue on dark navy — low contrast, hard to read (same issue in the Grade Report callout).
Column headers repeat the full chapter name on every column ('CHAPTER 1: FIRST STEPS' x N); a grouped/colspan chapter band would reduce noise across 92 columns.
Grid can only ever be as wide as the container, but at 1400px width only ~6 of 92 columns are visible with no visible horizontal scrollbar hint / 'scroll' affordance beyond the helper text.

action_items: Replace `bg-inherit` on the sticky student-name <td> with an opaque background so scrolled cells don't bleed through the frozen column.
Decide/confirm lesson_avg semantics for students with zero submissions (currently 0, shown red) vs blank.
Consider scoping the column set to the classroom's/teacher's curriculum instead of all db.problems (92 columns with duplicated chapter titles).
Improve contrast of the blue-on-navy info callout text.
critical_code_review_comments: get_gradebook_report queries db.problems with an empty filter and .to_list(20000) — unbounded full-collection scan on every request; scope by chapter/curriculum and/or project only needed fields with an index-backed filter.
submissions fetch uses .to_list(100000) and attempts .to_list(50000); with larger classes this can be memory heavy. Consider an aggregation pipeline ($group best score per student/problem) in Mongo.
/app/backend/server.py is 18k+ lines — the reports endpoints should be extracted into a router module.

rca_of_the_issue: Frozen-column bleed-through: the sticky <td> in TeacherReports.jsx line ~592 uses Tailwind `bg-inherit`, inheriting the <tr> background `bg-cyber-navy/40` (40% alpha). Because sticky elements paint above the scrolling content but with a translucent background, the underlying score cells remain visible through the frozen column. Repro: load gradebook for '2nd Period', scroll container horizontally, observe digits overlapping student names.
